subject: Merging by date results in C stack usage error

messages.author: 36d949fdb645491b
messages.subject: Merging by date results in C stack usage error
parts:
Hi,

I recently noticed an error that occurs when I use sqldf to merge two dataframes by date.

Try this example code:

#======================================

g <- data.frame(date=as.Date(c("1927-01-31","1927-02-28")),x=c(2,3))
h <- data.frame(date=as.Date(c("1927-01-31","1927-02-28")),y=c(4,5))
final <- sqldf("select d1.*, d2.y from g d1 left join h d2 on d1.date=d2.date")

#======================================

Looks simple but if I execute it, it fails with the error "Error: C stack usage is too close to the limit." If we do this in error=recover mode, we see a bunch of recursive calls to as.Date.numeric().

My session information:

R version 3.0.2 (2013-09-25)
Platform: x86_64-redhat-linux-gnu (64-bit)

attached base packages:
[1] tcltk stats graphics grDevices utils datasets methods
[8] base

other attached packages:
[1] sqldf_0.4-7 RSQLite.extfuns_0.0.1 RSQLite_0.11.4
[4] DBI_0.2-7 gsubfn_0.6-5 proto_0.3-10


This is a fresh install and I have not seen this error previously, so I'm thinking it might be a bug in a recent version of sqldf (or a related package).

Can anyone else reproduce it?

messages.author: 17e30776ec2a7fb1
messages.subject: Re: [sqldf] Merging by date results in C stack usage error
parts:
Unfortunately this bug was introduced in the latest update to sqldf.
It is fixed in the svn repo. Try this:

library(sqldf)
source("http://sqldf.googlecode.com/svn/trunk/R/sqldf.R")
# ... now run your code ...

or else use svn to get the development version and build it from source.
